newsitem.title: USA: Possis seeks expanded use of device.
newsitem.headline: Possis seeks expanded use of device.

text.p: Possis Medical Inc said Tuesday it asked the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to approve expanded use of its device which removes blood clots.

Possis is seeking approval to use its AngioJet Rapid Thrombectomy System to include use in peripheral arteries and bypass grafts in the United States. The application to the FDA includes results of studies in the U.S. and Germany on the use of the AngioJet System in leg arteries and bypass grafts.
In December 1996 the medical device company received its initial FDA clearance to market the AngioJet System to remove blood clots from dialysis access grafts.

A dialysis access graft is a tube implanted in the body connecting blood vessels. It is punctured regularly by a needle to connect a patient to a kidney dialysis machine. The graft is used to reduce bleeding and healing in frequent dialysis patients.

Possis said its technology is designed to remove blood clots from vessels throughout the body and therefore has potential to treat a wide range of serious medical conditions such as dialysis access graft failure, leg pain, heart attack and stroke.
The company said it expects a response to this latest FDA submission by mid-October.
Shares of Possis were trading off 1/8 to 15-5/8.
